solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Attractive worker takes part

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
some means a part of a whole

explanation.surface: A good-looking employee gets involved in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome is a common synonym for good-looking or attractive, especially of a person.

clue.text: Dash that makes Lee- Enfield double-barrelled

definitions.text: Dash that makes Lee- Enfield double-barrelled

parts.words: Dash that makes Lee- Enfield double-barrelled
parts.note: surface reading: something that turns a rifle into a two-barrelled gun

parts.words: Dash that makes Lee- Enfield double-barrelled
parts.note: setter's reading: the punctuation mark joining two names into one double-barrelled name

explanation.surface: A gun enthusiast wonders what makes a famous rifle into a double-barrelled weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lee-Enfield is a British army rifle; double-barrelled also describes a joined surname, which needs this mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This short punctuation dash links compound words and double-barrelled names.

clue.text: Phrase used to express admiration for bare minimum

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation, as in 'a knighthood
second meaning: not anything smaller, the least acceptable

explanation.walkthrough: The expression is said to show one is impressed, and literally means nothing smaller is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase signals being impressed, and its literal sense sets a floor below which nothing goes.

clue.text: Wise to have Cathedral City cheese

parts.note: sage means wise
Derby is an English city with a cathedral

explanation.surface: It is sensible to choose a branded Cathedral City cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cathedral City is also a well-known British brand of cheddar, which makes the surface read as shopping advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled green with sage leaves.

clue.text: Team ordering synthetic cream

indicators.note: ordering means putting into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports team puts in an order for artificial cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester City is an English Premier League football club, a sports team.

clue.text: About to analyse first something that's an astronomical length

indicators.note: first says the analysing word is placed at the front, ahead of the short word for about

parts.note: to parse is to analyse a sentence grammatically
c. (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to study something first, a scholar at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads About + to analyse, but first reorders them so the verb comes before the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is a unit of distance used in astronomy, about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: A counterpart that is similar

parts.note: taken as written
one's like is an equal or counterpart, as in 'we shall not see his like again'

explanation.surface: A matching partner turns out to resemble the original.
explanation.definitionFit: Alike means similar or resembling each other.

clue.text: Soldier from working party to fail

parts.note: a squad is a small team set to a task
an engine that fails is said to die

explanation.surface: A soldier is drawn from a work detail that is doomed to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaddie is British slang for a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A squaddie is an informal British term for a private soldier in the army.

clue.text: Top of the milk drink, rich fare

parts.note: cream rises to the top of unhomogenised milk
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: The best bit of milk goes into a drink, an indulgent snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of scones with clotted cream and jam, served with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a rich afternoon meal of scones, jam and clotted cream.

clue.text: Spread round large area of retail space

definitions.meaning: first meaning: scattered everywhere in disorder
second meaning: literally covering every part of a store

explanation.walkthrough: The informal British idiom means in a mess or scattered; read literally it describes the whole of a store.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered everywhere, and its literal sense is the full extent of a retail premises.

clue.text: Figure that parrot is missing as reported

indicators.note: as reported means as heard said, so the phrase is matched by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Polly is the stock name for a parrot, and gone means missing

explanation.surface: Someone reports how many birds have flown off from the pet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygon is a geometric figure, a closed plane shape with straight sides.

clue.text: Money certain to be spent in one's own time

parts.note: lei is the plural of leu, the currency of Romania
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Cash that is sure to be spent on free time.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time, the hours that belong to oneself rather than to work.

clue.text: Relaxed, having stopped hundred short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the hundred is taken away from the word for stopped

parts.note: ceased means stopped
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman calmed down after being out just short of a century.
explanation.walkthrough: CEASED loses its C to leave EASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased and relaxed are both past forms meaning loosened or made less tense.

clue.text: Move hoard over this blocking river

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are turned over and rearranged

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift a stockpile across something that blocks a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hoover Dam is the large dam on the Colorado River on the Arizona–Nevada border.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is a barrier blocking a river, and this is a famous American example.

clue.text: Angry way to interrogate

parts.note: cross means angry
to examine a witness is to question them

explanation.surface: A description of a bad-tempered style of questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and its words also build the answer: an angry word followed by a word for questioning; 'way to' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross-examine is to question a witness called by the other side in court, often in a hostile manner.

clue.text: Can let eye adjust to the gas

indicators.note: adjust asks for the letters to be moved about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Allowing one's vision to get used to a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: Type of education requiring bodily effort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: involving the body and strength

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of PE lessons, but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names the PE school subject and describes any strenuous activity of the body.

clue.text: Encounter amusing person who could be the knave

parts.note: to face is to confront or encounter
a card is a witty, amusing person

explanation.surface: Meeting a comedian who might turn out to be a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Knave reads as a scoundrel, but it is the jack in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Face cards are the king, queen and jack, and the knave is another name for the jack.

clue.text: Hard work made of it during storm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the idiom for struggling over a simple job and making it seem hard
second meaning: the rough conditions of a storm

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a loose description of conditions in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Making heavy weather of a task is an idiom for struggling needlessly; literally the phrase describes rough stormy conditions.

clue.text: From Jamaica, Jo learning to wheedle

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the island's name, the girl's name and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A Jamaican girl named Jo is learning to coax people.
explanation.definitionFit: To cajole is to persuade by flattery, which is what wheedling means.

clue.text: Ollie's partner's spoken a few lines

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the possessive name is matched by sound

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner was Stan Laurel
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel delivers a couple of lines of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were Stan and Ollie; 'Stan's a' said aloud gives the poetry term.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a verse of a poem.

clue.text: Show strange places, etc

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to display unusual locations and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a show or display, an impressive public performance.

clue.text: I'd let out that bathroom had been covered perhaps

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their usual places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A homeowner admits renting out a room that had been redecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The bathroom words only set the scene for how something might be covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiled means overlaid with tiles, one way a surface such as a bathroom wall is covered.

clue.text: You had a way with cause of ferment

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A compliment that the listener knew how to handle something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You had a way with' reads as praise for a knack; here had just means accompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that causes fermentation in brewing and baking.

clue.text: Diminutive fellow's garland?

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
-let is a suffix making things small, as in piglet or booklet

explanation.surface: A small man wears a wreath on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer looks like 'little chap', but it really means a wreath; the question mark admits the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or circlet of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: Gardened, now change for the dance

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a garden tool, so hoed means gardened

indicators.note: change asks for the word now to be altered into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having finished the gardening, someone changes clothes for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance or the social gathering where it is held.

clue.text: Youngster and I had article that's affectedly elegant

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
I'd is the contraction of I had
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boy and the speaker owned something posh.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da is an informal British term for pretentious or affectedly refined manners.

clue.text: Insects reaching edge in record time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Bugs arrive at the boundary in record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record time' looks like a single phrase meaning very fast; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera is the genus of mayflies, insects famous for living only a day as adults.
